quote: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal: The driver of a vehicle shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign, in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1], prior to entering an intersection if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto although not a part of a through highway and shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield and which are within the intersection or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

activation.condition: a stop or yield sign governs an entrance to the intersection and no police officer or traffic-control signal controls traffic

obligation.description: stop for a stop sign or yield for a yield sign in the manner of subsection 1 before entering; proceed cautiously and yield to vehicles not so obligated that are within or closely approaching the intersection

exceptions.trigger: traffic controlled by police officer or traffic-control signal
exceptions.effect: the subsection 2 signed-entrance duty is excepted while that control applies
exceptions.replacement_obligation: determine under the separately governing officer or signal direction
exceptions.source_clause: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:

timing.description: signed duty applies before entry; caution and priority continue while the driver moves across or within the intersection

judgment_calls_needed.note: A sign face and entrance governance need original Native and camera evidence.
Police direction or a controlling signal needs original Native and camera evidence.
The statute gives no numeric proximity or time-to-conflict cutoff.
Caution requires original motion and surroundings review, not a speed cutoff.
Stopping-reference order and visibility require authored-site and original-frame review.
